clue.text: Cathedral canons preach in turn around end of August

indicators.note: the reworked letters sit around the picked letter, holding it inside them
turning the word preach about reworks its letters into a new order
the end of a word is its final letter, here taken from August

explanation.surface: Senior clergy take turns delivering sermons as summer closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in turn' signals an anagram of PREACH (CHAPER), and 'around' wraps it round T, the last letter of August.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral's body of canons, its governing clergy, is formally called its chapter.

clue.text: Officer's murderer liable to be imprisoned

definitions.note: read as 'officer is', the 's linking to the wordplay

indicators.note: the second piece is locked inside the first

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis
apt means liable or likely to

explanation.surface: An officer's killer is likely to be jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: An army or navy officer rank, or the commander of a ship.

clue.text: Wine club recruiting church type who's normally abstemious

indicators.note: recruiting means taking in, so the church goes inside

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine
CE is the Church of England
C is the abbreviation for club, as in card suits

explanation.surface: A wine club signs up a churchgoer who rarely drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who practises severe self-denial for religious reasons lives austerely.

clue.text: Volunteers left on deck

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve
taken as written

explanation.surface: Volunteer sailors are left standing on the ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' is a pack of cards: in card games the talon is the undealt stock.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games the cards left after the deal form a pile drawn from during play.

clue.text: Welcome offered by east coast resort, quiet English town, originally

parts.note: Redcar is a seaside town on England's north-east coast
p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of town

explanation.surface: A warm reception laid on by a seaside place and a quiet English town.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial reception for an honoured guest, from the carpet unrolled for them.

clue.text: Cultural features in Financial Times-I mean!

indicators.note: the following pieces are placed inside the newspaper's initials

parts.note: FT is the standard abbreviation for the Financial Times newspaper
near means stingy or mean with money, a chiefly British sense

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that the arts pages are in the Financial Times, of all places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I plus NEAR inside FT. NEAR for 'mean' (tight-fisted) is an older British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Painting, sculpture and the like are the cultural works grouped under this phrase.

clue.text: Problem for soccer authorities last month

parts.note: the FA, Football Association, runs English football
ult., ultimo, means last month in old business letters

explanation.surface: Football's governing body had trouble last month.
explanation.definitionFit: A defect or flaw that causes trouble.

clue.text: Hour being struck — next one

indicators.note: struck means hit and knocked about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The clock strikes the hour and the next one follows.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'Hour being' rearrange exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: The person living next door is the one beside you.

clue.text: Dark green case, one there's a fuss about

indicators.note: about means around, so a fuss wraps the other pieces

parts.note: ado is fuss, as in much ado about nothing
voc. is the abbreviation for vocative, a grammatical case
A is one, as in a or one item

explanation.surface: Someone makes a fuss over a dark green case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts VOC and A inside ADO, splitting it A...DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull deep green colour named after the pear-shaped fruit's skin.

clue.text: One of two letters found in grass"?

explanation.surface: A question about letters turning up in grass.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'letters' are epistles: the New Testament has two addressed to this disciple of Paul.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul's epistles 1 and 2 to a young follower bear his name; it is also a pasture grass grown for hay.

clue.text: Choice items were first preserved in vinegar

parts.note: the pick of a crop is its choicest items
led means were in front, came first

explanation.surface: The best produce was the first to go into the vinegar jars.
explanation.definitionFit: Food kept in brine or vinegar is described this way, like onions or gherkins.

clue.text: Unvarying habit

explanation.surface: A routine that never changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Unchanging throughout is one sense; a habit is distinctive dress, such as a nun's or a soldier's regulation outfit.

clue.text: Page possibly attached to last section, to finish a set of books

indicators.note: the remaining pieces come at the finish, after the others

parts.note: att. is a standard abbreviation for attached
the end is the final section of anything
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A note about binding: the closing section is fixed on to complete a multi-volume set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Page' is a person here, a young servant, not a sheet of a book; 'possibly' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A page is a boy employed to wait on someone, one kind of servant who waits on people.

clue.text: Spirit that's central to the arts

indicators.note: the letters are found in the centre of the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: A claim that soul is what matters most in creative work.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage or enthusiasm, as in 'put your heart into it', is a sense of spirit.

clue.text: Suitable place for hospital in resort

indicators.note: the letter for hospital is placed inside the resort's name

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Looking for a good site to build a hospital in a holiday town.
explanation.definitionFit: A position that suits someone perfectly, as in finding one's place in life.

clue.text: Vermivorous pterosaur?

parts.note: a worm-eating flier from long ago, taken literally from the proverb about catching the worm

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gets up early; the proverbial bird that rises first catches the worm.

clue.text: Factor only present initially in oocyte, endlessly involved in reproduction

parts.note: pH is the acidity factor, as in pH-balanced shampoo

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the gathered letters are mixed together
initially picks the opening letter of each of the words only and present
endlessly drops the last letter of oocyte

explanation.surface: A biology note on something found only in an egg cell and involved in reproduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' scrambles PH, O and P (the first letters of 'only present') and OOCYT ('oocyte' without its end).
explanation.definitionFit: A copy made on a copying machine is a reproduction of the original.

clue.text: Drier in the south-east

parts.note: reads as a weather forecast but means a building for drying hops in Kent

explanation.definitionFit: A kiln for drying hops, typical of Kent in south-east England.

clue.text: Secretary engaged by an ineffectual person needs American equipment

parts.note: an gives the letter A

indicators.note: engaged means held, so the secretary is held inside the other pieces

parts.note: prat is British slang for a foolish, useless person
PA, personal assistant, is a secretary

explanation.surface: An office assistant working for a hopeless boss needs American gear.
explanation.walkthrough: PA goes inside A PRAT, giving APPARAT; US follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparatus is the gear or kit needed for a task.

clue.text: Try getting casual worker in a couple of times

indicators.note: the worker is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, so two of them
a temp is a temporary worker

explanation.surface: A temp gets a second try at the job.
explanation.definitionFit: An effort to do something, a go.

clue.text: A little Seneca, typically

parts.note: looks like a snippet of the Roman philosopher, but means a small child of the Seneca Native American people

explanation.definitionFit: A Native American baby, often carried on the back; the Seneca are an Iroquois nation.

clue.text: Keen to pursue artist's offer

indicators.note: the offer follows on behind the artist

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword's usual artist
a bid is an offer, as at an auction

explanation.surface: An eager buyer chases the price a painter asks.
explanation.definitionFit: Fanatically enthusiastic, as a rabid fan is.

clue.text: Metal easily crushed by one's thumb?

indicators.note: crushed means squashed out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: one's is I'S, I being one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A soft metal that crumbles under a thumb.
explanation.definitionFit: A brittle, pinkish-white chemical element with symbol Bi.

clue.text: Swimmer's record, hard one for fellow to accept

definitions.note: read as 'swimmer is', the 's linking to the wordplay

indicators.note: accept means take in, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: a don is a university fellow
LP, long-player, is a record
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A swimmer's record time, a tough one for a college fellow to accept.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea mammal famous for its swimming.

clue.text: What waiter gets -ultimately, jolly drunk

parts.note: tips are the extra money a waiter receives

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, picking the last letter of jolly

explanation.surface: A waiter's gratuity ends with him merry and drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly intoxicated, a mild word for the effects of drink.

clue.text: Company practice

parts.note: reads as a firm's business custom but means a run-through by a theatre company before the show

explanation.definitionFit: Actors in a company practise their play in a run-through before opening night.

clue.text: German encountered in northern French city, mostly a divergent type

indicators.note: the German is met inside the shortened city name
mostly drops the last letter

parts.note: Rouen is a city in Normandy

explanation.surface: A German met in Rouen turned out to be an oddball.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal or person that deviates from the group, like a rogue elephant.

clue.text: Croat, versatile player

indicators.note: versatile means adaptable, turning in many ways, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Croatian performer who can play many parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer on stage or screen plays a role.

clue.text: Low tone from bell in ship's berth

parts.note: to low is to moo, the sound of cattle
a bell's ring is its tone

explanation.surface: A deep note from a bell rings out where a ship is docked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' is the verb for a cow's call, not 'deep'.
explanation.definitionFit: The place where a ship is tied up is its berth.

clue.text: Pork pie and nut chewed by girl

indicators.note: by means beside, the girl's name standing next to the other piece
something chewed is mangled, so the word nut is rearranged

parts.note: Ruth is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl munching a pork pie and a nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pork pie' is Cockney rhyming slang for 'lie', so it is the definition, not food. The anagram of NUT is UNT.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang a pork pie is a lie, a falsehood.

clue.text: Lever in plane, possibly, lad's broken

indicators.note: the jumbled lad goes inside the tree

parts.note: a plane is one kind of tree

indicators.note: broken means the letters of lad are smashed and rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A boy has broken a lever on an aeroplane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' suggests an aircraft, but it is the plane tree; 'broken' turns LAD into ADL inside TREE.
explanation.definitionFit: A foot-operated lever that drives a machine, such as an old sewing machine.

clue.text: Ceramic art collected by oriental woman

indicators.note: collected means held, so the art goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: E for east, oriental meaning eastern
hen is slang for a woman, especially in Scotland
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Eastern woman has collected pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Made of baked clay, as pottery is.
